findings.evidence: template/scripts/github_read_cache.py `_page`: the comment says "A last page (no stored ``next``) is always re-read", and the code only adds `-H If-None-Match` when `entry is not None and entry["next"] is not None`. A 304 on a last page also raises GithubReadError. `get_json` without paginate, as used by `managed_task.fetch_issue`, always fetches a single page whose `next` is None, so it is never conditional. Contract text: chat-coordinator spec says the cache is "revalidated by ETag on every read" and the Repeated-overview scenario says "spends only conditional requests that return 304 plus a bounded number of counted requests". The lifecycle-workers scenario says "it spends conditional requests rather than counted re-reads for unchanged PRs". design.md says "Its Issue read is conditional instead" and "each page conditional"; proposal.md says "revalidated by ETag (conditional request) on every read". tests/test_github_read_cache.py `test_warm_read_is_conditional_...` asserts (counted, conditional) == (3, 1) on a warm read, which confirms the last page is re-fetched at full cost. The implementation also contradicts the design's "whole-body entries ... 304 returns the complete stored body" model for last pages, and the design never documents the always-re-read rule.
findings.summary: The cache never sends If-None-Match for a response without a `Link: rel="next"`, i.e. any single-page read. That covers most PR comment histories, the PR list, the open-Requirement listing and every Requirement Issue read via `fetch_issue`. Those reads are always full counted requests. This contradicts the spec and design, which say every read is revalidated by ETag and an unchanged issue costs no counted request.
